commit: 79837f3 fix(menubar): keep attention bubble attached to pet during drag
problem: Dragging the floating pet (Maew) while an attention bubble is displayed detaches the bubble: it stays pinned at its old anchor instead of tracking the pet during the drag.
solution: Route every panel frame change (drag translate + resize) through a single handleFrameChange sink in FloatingPetPanelController that updates lastPanelFrame and re-anchors the attention bubble while attention is active, then forwards to the external persistence handler. Previously lastPanelFrame and bubble reposition only happened inside show(), so mid-drag frame emits never re-anchored the bubble. Do not reintroduce a raw external frameChangeHandler wired straight to the interaction view — it bypasses the bubble re-anchor.
prompt_lesson: For any draggable/resizable container, enumerate every child or attached overlay (bubbles, badges, affordances, pills) and assert each tracks the same transform. Coordinate-space cohesion is the UI analogue of cross-file-atomicity: a multi-part visual whole must move atomically. Caveat: only review-reachable when the container's drag handler and the attached overlay live in the same ticket diff — here the floating pet (P4) and attention bubble (P6) shipped in different phases, so the per-ticket review for neither had both halves in view. That cross-ticket blindness is itself the finding: integration-of-features bugs need a phase-level review pass, not just per-ticket.
test_reachability: Weak. The bug is integration behavior: a real NSPanel drag emitting frame changes while an AttentionBubblePanel is live. BubbleLayout.frame is a pure function and was already correct; the regression was the missing *call* on drag. A faithful unit test needs a real panel + drag simulation, which the existing FloatingPetPanelSpy (used by controller tests) does not exercise. Verified instead by build + manual drag QA. This is a representative experiential/integration miss.
recurrence: see codogotchi-02+ for other coordinate-space coupling, e.g. phase-04 fix-08 screen-space grab offset
